judiciary_advocateconsole.a_short_label_: A short label for this filing
judiciary_advocateconsole.advocate_regis: Advocate registration is open to any associated resident, but a court must exist in your jurisdiction first — courts form when a legislature creates one (F-LEG-017).
judiciary_advocateconsole.cases_you_file: Cases you file on behalf of clients appear here.
Cases you filed on behalf of clients (via F-ADV-001).
judiciary_advocateconsole.entity_state_m: Entity state machine: Case — filings attach at specific states (motions before and during hearing, evidence on the open docket, briefs until deliberation); the case detail page plays the full sequence. The attach-window is enforced by the engine, not this page.
judiciary_advocateconsole.no_judiciary_i: No judiciary in your association chain yet.
judiciary_advocateconsole.recorded_with_: Recorded with your registration; the bar's competence is a property of the bar, never a gate on your client's right.
judiciary_advocateconsole.register_as_an: Register as an advocate (F-IND-015) to file on behalf of a client.
judiciary_advocateconsole.representation: Representation is a constitutional right of your clients; registration keeps the bar of advocates zealous and competent. Registration is open to any associated resident — association with the court's jurisdiction is the only eligibility check.
judiciary_advocateconsole.what_this_fili: What this filing asks the court to do
judiciary_advocateconsole.workflows_regi: Workflows: registration is WF-CIV-07; every filing feeds the WF-JUD-03 case lifecycle.
judiciary_advocateconsole.your_client_re: Your client retains you; the retainer is recorded with the filing.
judiciary_advocateconsole.your_docketed_: Your docketed filings appear here — the docket is append-only; nothing is ever sealed retroactively (Art. IV §4).
judiciary_advocateconsole.your_filings_m: Your filings, motions, evidence, and briefs — everything you submit lands on the public docket of the case it belongs to. Representation is a constitutional right of your clients; registration keeps the bar of advocates zealous and competent.
judiciary_casedetail.access_controlled_r: Access-controlled room for the panel judges only. Parties and advocates cannot enter.
judiciary_casedetail.an_arrest_warrant_m: An arrest warrant must state the maximum duration · Art. II §8.
judiciary_casedetail.commentary_on_the_l: Commentary on the law as written or edited; only the Art. IV §5 process changes a law's text.
judiciary_casedetail.criminal_outcome_ca: — criminal outcome carries the double-jeopardy flag · Art. II §8
judiciary_casedetail.every_warrant_must_: Every warrant must establish its reason · Art. II §8.
judiciary_casedetail.issues_only_on_a_gu: Issues only on a guilty criminal verdict · Art. IV §4.
judiciary_casedetail.jurors_alternates_d: {jurors} jurors + {alternates} alternates drawn at random from {pool_label}. The selection seed is published to the audit chain — anyone can verify the draw.
judiciary_casedetail.no_exhibits_on_the_: No exhibits on the evidence docket.
judiciary_casedetail.no_jury_a_jury_atta: No jury — a jury attaches only to a jury-entitled criminal case.
judiciary_casedetail.no_pre_trial_motion: No pre-trial motions on the docket.
judiciary_casedetail.on_a_guilty_verdict: On a guilty verdict the panel issues a sentencing order (F-JDG-009); any arrest, search, or seizure connected to enforcement needs a warrant with a stated reason and duration (F-JDG-010 · Art. II §8). The court's actions render below.
judiciary_casedetail.opinion_linked_as_c: Opinion linked as commentary · Art. IV §4–§5
judiciary_casedetail.random_draw_complet: Random draw complete — voir dire under way
judiciary_casedetail.see_how_a_finding_c: See how a finding changes the law — the Art. IV §5 tracker →
judiciary_casedetail.see_this_stage_as_a: See this stage as a summoned juror →
judiciary_casedetail.separate_deliberati: Separate deliberation preserves the independence of the jury of peers · Art. IV §4
judiciary_casedetail.the_bench_is_seated: The bench is seated when the court accepts the case and classifies severity (F-JDG-001). Conflicted judges are excluded and the draw re-runs.
judiciary_casedetail.the_case_lifecycle_: The case lifecycle is WF-JUD-03; jury paneling is WF-JUD-04; a constitutional finding branches into WF-JUD-05. Major constitutional questions take the full court instead of a severity-scaled panel (CLK-16, hardened). The Case state machine renders live above.
judiciary_casedetail.the_court_advances_: The court advances the append-only record by filing through the engine — each action is accepted only at the state where it is legal (the engine is the boundary). Art. IV §4.
judiciary_casedetail.the_court_s_classif: The court's classification drives the panel size — not the filer's claim.
judiciary_casedetail.the_jury_deliberate: The jury deliberates separately — no judges, no parties, no contact. Deliberation is the only unrecorded space; the verdict itself is recorded.
judiciary_casedetail.the_panel_publishes: The panel publishes its opinion to the public record, linked to the case and to every law it interprets. Opinions are commentary on the law as written or edited — only the Art. IV §5 process can change the law's text.
judiciary_casedetail.the_public_record_o: The public record of one case before the court — every filing, ruling, and the panel that hears it. This page renders the live record and the surrounding context; the court advances the append-only record by acting through the engine, never a toggle.
judiciary_casedetail.the_selection_seed_: The selection seed publishes to the audit chain — anyone can verify the draw · Art. IV §4.
judiciary_casedetail.this_criminal_case_: This criminal case is jury-entitled — the jury is drawn at random once the bench is seated (F-JDG-002). The selection seed publishes to the audit chain.
judiciary_casedetail.whichever_way_the_v: Whichever way the verdict falls, the outcome record carries the double-jeopardy flag: the accused can never be prosecuted again for this same accusation. The flag is machine-enforced at filing time.
judiciary_casedocket.civil_criminal_case: Civil/criminal case filing · F-IND-017 → F-JDG-001 · the court classifies justiciability and severity, then assigns a panel with conflict screening · Art. IV §4 · Art. I (Right to Fair Trial)
judiciary_casedocket.conflict_screening_: Conflict screening: before a panel is fixed, every candidate judge is screened for personal, financial, or prior-involvement conflicts; conflicted judges are excluded and the draw re-runs. Screening results attach to the case record.
judiciary_casedocket.e_g_okafor_v_crown_: e.g. Okafor v. Crown Ridge LLC
judiciary_casedocket.every_case_filed_in: Every case filed in this court, from local civil disputes to full-court constitutional questions. Anyone who lives here (a verified resident) can file; panels are assigned by the court with conflict screening.
judiciary_casedocket.filing_states_a_cla: Filing states a claimed scale (which jurisdiction's law is at issue, so the right court level hears it) and a claimed severity (which the court reclassifies on acceptance). You can file yourself or through a registered advocate.
judiciary_casedocket.no_cases_match_the_: No cases match the current filters.
judiciary_casedocket.no_cases_on_this_do: No cases on this docket — anyone jurisdictionally associated can file (Art. I).
judiciary_casedocket.open_cases_with_kin: Open cases with kind, court, panel, severity, and state
judiciary_casedocket.panel_assignment_wi: Panel assignment with conflict screening · full court for major constitutional questions · Art. IV §4 · CLK-16
judiciary_casedocket.panels_of_at_least_: Panels of at least 3, odd, scaled to severity · full court for major constitutional questions · Art. IV §4 · CLK-16
judiciary_casedocket.reference_cards_the: Reference cards — the filing instruments that open a case from a different door.
judiciary_casedocket.the_case_lifecycle_: The case lifecycle (WF-JUD-03) carries every filing from a claimed scale and severity through acceptance, panel assignment with conflict screening, hearing, and judgement. Constitutional challenges branch into the Art. IV §5 tracker (WF-JUD-05); jury paneling runs as WF-JUD-04. The Case state machine:
judiciary_casedocket.the_court_reclassif: The court reclassifies severity at acceptance — panel size follows the court's classification, not yours.
judiciary_casedocket.the_docket_is_publi: The docket is public to read. Filing a case is open to anyone jurisdictionally associated (Art. I) — confirm your residency to unlock filing. Confirm residency →
judiciary_casedocket.the_jurisdiction_wh: The jurisdiction whose law the case arises under.
judiciary_casedocket.walk_a_case_through: Walk a case through the full lifecycle →
judiciary_casedocket.what_happened_and_w: What happened, and what remedy you seek
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.any_in: Any inhabitant can challenge a law that unjustly impedes their rights. When the court finds a contradiction, three resolution paths open: the legislature amends, the legislature overrides by supermajority within the veto window, or — if the window closes with neither — the judiciary edits the law directly. A finding, a recommended fix, a reasonable timeframe to act, and an override window — all on a public clock.
Any inhabitant may file; no standing gatekeeper beyond jurisdictional association — the right is absolute and fee-free (Art. IV §5.1 · Art. I).
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.confir: Confirm a residency to file a challenge
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.how_th: How the law impedes your rights
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.no_fee: no fee, no eligibility ground, no standing gatekeeper — the engine enforces the absolute right and parks the filing at when no court is yet seated · F-IND-016 · Art. IV §5.1 · Art. I
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.readin: Reading is open to everyone — findings, remedies, and every member's override position are public record (Art. II §2). Filing a challenge needs an active residency association with the jurisdiction whose law you challenge (R-03). Confirm residency →
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.select: — select an in-force or amended law —
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.the_ar: The Article/Section the law contradicts, if you can name it.
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.the_ch: The challenge is its own durable entity, distinct from the case it is heard in: the CLK-11/CLK-12 windows run for weeks-to-months after the hearing closes, gated on legislature action. Resolved court: {name}.
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.the_co: The court reads this; there is no merits test at filing — the right to be heard is absolute.
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.the_la: The law's binding jurisdiction or a descendant under it that you inhabit.
judiciary_constitutionalchallenge.workfl: Workflows: — constitutional challenge & law remedy; hearings run on the WF-JUD-03 machinery; Path A re-enters the bill flow (WF-LEG-06); executives enforce the outcome (WF-EXE-07).
judiciary_home.an_independent_court_serv: An independent court serving this jurisdiction and its constituents. Created by supermajority act of the legislature; judges nominated by the constituent jurisdictions in equal numbers (or the judicial committee as fallback) and confirmed by consent vote. Appointed is the default kind of court — converting it to an elected court takes two separate supermajorities.
judiciary_home.appointed_judges_hold_a_y: Appointed judges hold a {years}-year term ({clk}); converted elected judges instead run in lockstep with the general election ({civilLockstep}).
judiciary_home.civil_judicial_appointmen: civil + judicial appointment lengths move in lockstep · Art. IV §1 · Art. II §9
judiciary_home.confirmation_needs_the_sa: Confirmation needs the same threshold the creation act met; one consent vote is held per nominee. Constituents keep their nomination rights; replacement nominees go to a fresh consent vote when a seat next opens (WF-JUD-07).
judiciary_home.confirmation_record_conse: Confirmation record — consent votes for the bench
judiciary_home.constituent_jurisdictions: Constituent jurisdictions nominate equal numbers; judicial committee as fallback · Art. IV §2
judiciary_home.conversion_adopted_on_the: Conversion adopted on the chamber supermajority alone
judiciary_home.converting_this_appointed: Converting this appointed court to a directly elected one needs two independent supermajorities: the legislature's own, and a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions themselves. Neither alone is enough.
judiciary_home.introduce_a_conversion_bi: Introduce a conversion bill → filed by a member of the source legislature (R-09)
judiciary_home.introduce_a_creation_bill: Introduce a creation bill → filed by a member of the source legislature (R-09)
judiciary_home.judicial_nomination_conse: Judicial nomination consent vote, one per nominee · F-LEG-021 · Art. IV §2
Judicial nomination consent votes, one per nominee
judiciary_home.no_conversion_on_record_i: No conversion on record. If conversion passes, judges are thereafter elected in groups of at least {min_judges_per_race} via STV, and judicial terms sync to the general election clock (Art. IV §3 · CLK-15 · CLK-10).
judiciary_home.no_creation_act_on_record: No creation act on record — this judiciary is a constitutional placeholder. The legislature creates the court by supermajority act, deriving the nomination mode from the jurisdiction's constituent structure (Art. IV §1–§2).
judiciary_home.no_direct_constituent_jur: No direct constituent jurisdiction holds a legislature able to vote, so the conversion completes on the chamber's own supermajority (Art. IV §3). A judicial election schedules from here.
judiciary_home.no_nominations_on_record_: No nominations on record yet. Once the creation act passes, each constituent (or the judicial committee) nominates a judge onto a vacant seat, and each nomination flows into its own F-LEG-021 consent vote.
judiciary_home.one_judiciary_row_per_jur: One judiciary row per jurisdiction with a legislature — the same row evolves through its lifecycle (Art. IV §1–§3). There is no per-case entity behind this surface; cases live on the docket.
judiciary_home.panel_sizing_is_a_hard_co: panel sizing is a hard constraint · CLK-16 · Art. IV §4
judiciary_home.panels_of_at_least_3_odd_: Panels of at least 3, odd, scaled to severity; full court for major constitutional questions · Art. IV §4 · CLK-16 — elected judges (if converted) run in groups of at least {min_judges_per_race} · Art. IV §4 · CLK-15
judiciary_home.severity_scaling_the_heav: Severity scaling: the heavier the possible consequence, the more judges must hear it — the panel is always odd so no case can deadlock.
judiciary_home.supermajority_of_legislat: Supermajority of legislature + supermajority of constituent jurisdictions · Art. IV §3 — groups of at least {min_judges_per_race} per race · CLK-15 · Art. IV §4 — terms synced · CLK-10
judiciary_home.supermajority_two_thirds_: Supermajority: two thirds of all serving members — counted against everyone holding a seat, never just those present (ceil(serving × 2/3) · Art. VII).
judiciary_home.term_sync_on_the_chamber_: term sync on the chamber page →
judiciary_home.the_judiciary_is_created_: The judiciary is created by supermajority act and exists as a stub from the moment a jurisdiction with a legislature is set up. The appointed footing is the default — conversion to a directly elected court is the only path to elected judges, and it is deliberately hard: a supermajority of the chamber AND a supermajority of the constituent jurisdictions must each agree (Art. IV §3). Every meter on this page is the engine's own snapshot — never a demo toggle.
judiciary_home.the_supermajority_that_ch: The supermajority that chartered the court
judiciary_home.this_court_s_seat_were_no: This court's {judge_count} seat{creation} were nominated by {nominationModeLabel}. Equal numbers from each constituent jurisdiction are mandatory; where a constituent declines, the legislature's judicial committee supplies the nomination in its stead.
judiciary_jurorview.art_ii_8_is_the_cons: Art. II §8 is the constitution's list of actions forbidden to legislatures — these two subsections shield jurors from both interference and charges.
judiciary_jurorview.draw_integrity_the_r: Draw integrity: the random-selection seed is published to the audit chain — anyone can verify the draw
judiciary_jurorview.no_fees_ever_no_paym: No fees, ever. No payment, fee, or fine can be required of you to exercise a civic right or fulfill this obligation — attendance, filings, and verification cost you nothing.
judiciary_jurorview.no_interference_your: No interference. Your employer cannot penalize, dismiss, or obstruct you for serving; nobody — public or private — may impede a civic obligation.
judiciary_jurorview.see_the_case_this_su: See the case this summons belongs to
judiciary_jurorview.the_deliberation_roo: The deliberation room is access-controlled: jurors only. The jury deliberates separately from the judges' chambers, with no contact from parties, advocates, or judges. Deliberation is the only unrecorded space in the trial — the verdict itself is recorded.
judiciary_jurorview.the_room_unlocks_at_: The room unlocks at the deliberation stage
judiciary_jurorview.you_were_drawn_at_ra: You were drawn at random from the eligible pool of verified residents. Service is a protected civic obligation — nobody can interfere with it, and nothing about it can ever cost you a fee.
